title: Easiest Cookie Icing
creator: Rocketmandee (Mandy, Happiness is Homemade)
servings: Not specified (the creator says a couple teaspoons of corn syrup spreads over 24+ cookies)
ingredients: 4-5 tablespoons water (milk or half-and-half also work; see notes)
instructions: Step 1: Put all the ingredients except the water in a bowl and whisk together.
Step 2: Add the water slowly while whisking, adding more only if you want to thin the icing out.
Step 3: If you add too much water, whisk in more powdered sugar until it reaches the thickness you want.
notes: From a Rocketmandee Facebook reel ('The best cookie icing out there!'); the full recipe comes from the creator's printable recipe on her blog (https://rocketmandee.com/2026/10/27/cookie-icing/). It is technically a glaze but works as cookie icing: it hardens enough to stack cookies without getting rock hard. Creator notes: milk is a good substitute for the water, and some people like half-and-half; use clear vanilla to keep the icing stark white (regular vanilla adds a slight brown tint); gel or liquid food coloring both work; you can pipe, spoon, spread with a knife or offset spatula, or dip the cookies; thin it further with more liquid for a glaze for donuts, cakes, or cookies. Corn syrup adds sheen and helps the icing stick, but it turns out fine without it. She pairs it with her Classic No Spread Cut Out Sugar Cookies recipe on the same blog.
